propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui ad illustrandam Ecclesiam tuam beatum Canutum regem martyrii palma
et gloriosis miraculis decorare dignatus es: concede propitius; ut, sicut
ipse dominicae passionis imitator fuit, ita nos, per ejus vestigia
gradientes, ad gaudia sempiterna pervenire mereamur. Per eundem Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n872, printed p. 874, under `Commemoration of St. Canute` and `Prayer`. The facing Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer apart from the compositor's `Domincae`; Canute is printed by name in both columns.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O God, Who for the enlightenment of Thy Church didst vouchsafe to distinguish blessed King Canute with the palm of martyrdom and with glorious miracles, mercifully grant, that as he was an imitator of the Lord's passion, so we, walking in his footsteps, may deserve to enter into everlasting joys. Through our Lord.

Accepta sit in conspectu tuo, Domine, nostra devotio: et ejus nobis fiat
supplicatione salutaris, pro cujus solemnitate defertur. Per Dominum
nostrum.

propers.text:
Refecti participatione muneris sacri, quaesumus, Domine Deus noster: ut,
cujus exsequimur cultum, intercedente beato Canuto Martyre tuo, sentiamus
effectum. Per Dominum.
